editorial_rule: A lemma statement contains only its quantified objects, hypotheses, and conclusion. It contains no motivation, derivation, commentary, proof sketch, interpretation, history, or explanation; put all such material in the proof.

lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the weighted-restriction fact in the exact external package recorded from KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.5–2.7 and 6.1–6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $d,D$ be nonnegative integers, let $A\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ have $(1,1,d)$-weighted degree at most $D$, let $L$ be an affine line equipped with an affine bijection $\ell_L:\mathbb{F}_p\to L$, and let $P_L\in\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ have degree at most $d$. Then $\deg_t A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\le D$.
lemmas.title: Weighted restriction degree

lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the base-polynomial line bound in the exact external package recorded from KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.5–2.7 and 6.1–6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $H\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ be nonzero and have total degree at most $D$. If $\mathcal{R}$ is a set of affine lines, each equipped with an affine parametrization $\ell_L$, and $H(\ell_L(t))\equiv 0$ for every $L\in\mathcal{R}$, then $|\mathcal{R}|\le D$.
lemmas.title: Base-line vanishing bound

lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the coprime graph-line bound in the exact external package recorded from KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.5–2.7 and 6.1–6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $F,G\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ be coprime polynomials of total degrees $u$ and $v$. If $\mathcal{S}$ is a collection of polynomial graph lines $(L,P_L)$ such that $F(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0$ and $G(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0$ for every $(L,P_L)\in\mathcal{S}$, then $|\mathcal{S}|\le uv$.
lemmas.title: Coprime graph-line intersection

lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the simple-root Newton-lifting fact in the exact external package recorded from KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.5–2.7 and 6.1–6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $B\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$, let $b=(b_1,b_2)\in\mathbb{F}_p^2$, and let $z_0\in\mathbb{F}_p$ satisfy $B(b_1,b_2,z_0)=0$ and $B_Z(b_1,b_2,z_0)\ne 0$. Then there is a unique formal power series $q\in\mathbb{F}_p[[U,V]]$ satisfying $q(0,0)=z_0$ and $B(b_1+U,b_2+V,q(U,V))=0$.
lemmas.title: Formal Newton lifting

lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the incident-line polynomialization fact in the exact external package recorded from KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.5–2.7 and 6.1–6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $B\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ have $(1,1,d)$-weighted degree at most $D$, and let $(b,z_0)$ be a simple $Z$-root of $B$. If more than $D$ distinct polynomial graph lines through $(b,z_0)$, whose graph polynomials have degree at most $d$, carry formal identities for $B$ compatible with the formal Newton lift through $(b,z_0)$, then there exists $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv 0$ and the restriction of $Q$ to each of those graph lines is its graph polynomial.
lemmas.title: Incident-line polynomialization

lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the simple-root propagation fact in the exact external package recorded from KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.5–2.7 and 6.1–6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected accepted bipartite component whose line vertices carry polynomial graph labels of degree at most $d$. Suppose $B$ vanishes formally on every line graph in $\Gamma$, every accepted incidence is a simple $Z$-root of $B$, and $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ has total degree at most $d$ and satisfies $B(X,Y,Q)\equiv 0$. If there is a point vertex $b$ such that $Q(\ell_L(t))\equiv P_L(t)$ for every line vertex $L$ adjacent to $b$, then $Q(\ell_L(t))\equiv P_L(t)$ for every line vertex $L$ of $\Gamma$, and $Q(x)=f(x)$ for every point vertex $x$ of $\Gamma$.
lemmas.title: Connected-component propagation

lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the sole assumed mathematical statement. The strict rank inequality asserts the existence of a nonzero kernel element, rather than failure of surjectivity. The reaching points are distinct, and each uses a selected line $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$ different from $L$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Fix $\theta$ with $0<\theta\le 1/4$, constants $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge 1$, and constants $a_\theta,c_\theta$ with $0<a_\theta,c_\theta\le 1$ and $C_\theta\ge 8K_\theta/a_\theta$. The hypothesis $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$ asserts the following. For every prime $p$, every integer $d$ with $100<d<p$, every function $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$, and every family indexed by all affine lines $L$ consisting of an affine bijection $\ell_L:\mathbb{F}_p\to L$ and a polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$, define

$$E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\{(\ell_L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(\ell_L(t))\},\qquad \varepsilon=\frac{|E_{\mathrm{acc}}|}{p^2(p+1)},$$

and

$$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y],\,\deg(Q)\le d}\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)].$$

For an integer $D\ge 0$, let

$$V_D=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{F}_p}\{X^iY^jZ^k:i+j+dk\le D\},$$

and, for a set $R$ of affine lines, let

$$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\longrightarrow\prod_{M\in R}\mathbb{F}_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\longmapsto\bigl(A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$

Whenever $\varepsilon\ge C_\theta(d/p)^{1-\theta}$, either $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta\varepsilon$, or there exist an accepted bipartite subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$ with $E\subseteq E_{\mathrm{acc}}$, a set $R\subseteq T$, and an integer $D$ such that

$$\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}\ge a_\theta\varepsilon,\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d,\qquad |R|>D,$$

$$\operatorname{rank}(\Phi_{R,D})<\dim(V_D),$$

and, for every $L\in T$, more than $D$ distinct points $x$ satisfy $(x,L)\in E$ and $(x,M)\in E$ for some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$.
lemmas.title: Rank-or-decode hypothesis

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Put $\rho=d/p$ and $x=D/p$. The threshold and the upper bound on $D$ give

$$x\le \frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\varepsilon\rho^\theta\le \frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{8}\le \frac18.$$

Hence $D<p$. Moreover,

$$x^2+3x\le \frac{25x}{8}\le \frac{25a_\theta\varepsilon}{64}<\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2}.$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Fix $0<\theta\le 1/4$, $K_\theta\ge 1$, $0<a_\theta\le 1$, and $C_\theta\ge 8K_\theta/a_\theta$. Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$ and $d\le D\le K_\theta d$ be integers, and let $0<\varepsilon\le 1$ satisfy $\varepsilon\ge C_\theta(d/p)^{1-\theta}$. Then

$$D<p\qquad\text{and}\qquad \left(\frac Dp\right)^2+3\frac Dp<\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2}.$$
lemmas.title: Characteristic and deletion budget

lemmas.proof_markdown: The strict rank inequality gives a nonzero $A_0\in\ker(\Phi_{R,D})$. Replace $A_0$ by its squarefree radical $A=\operatorname{rad}(A_0)$. Every selected graph identity survives because $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ is a domain, and the weighted degree does not increase. If $A$ were independent of $Z$, the defining linear polynomial of each of the $|R|>D$ selected lines would divide the nonzero base polynomial $A$, contradicting the base-line bound recorded in P0. Thus $A$ is $Z$-dependent. Since $\deg_Z(A)\le D<p$, the equality $A_Z=0$ would force $A$ to be independent of $Z$. Therefore $A_Z\ne 0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
In the structured alternative of $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$, suppose $D<p$. Then there exists a nonzero squarefree polynomial $A\in V_D$ that is $Z$-dependent and satisfies

$$A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\equiv 0\qquad\text{for every }M\in R,$$

and $A_Z\ne 0$.
lemmas.title: Squarefree kernel relation

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix $L\in T$, and let $x$ be one of its reaching points. Choose $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$ witnessing that point, and choose $t_L,t_M\in\mathbb{F}_p$ with $\ell_L(t_L)=x=\ell_M(t_M)$. Acceptedness gives

$$P_L(t_L)=f(x)=P_M(t_M),$$

while the selected graph identity gives $A(\ell_M(t_M),P_M(t_M))=0$. Hence $t_L$ is a root of $A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))$. This restriction has degree at most $D$ and has more than $D$ distinct roots, so it is identically zero.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $A$ be the relation obtained in P3. Suppose that, for every $L\in T$, more than $D$ distinct points $x$ satisfy $(x,L)\in E$ and $(x,M)\in E$ for some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$. Then

$$A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0\qquad\text{for every }L\in T.$$
lemmas.title: Reached-root extension

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Because $A$ is squarefree and $A=HB$, the quotient $B$ is squarefree; because $H$ is independent of $Z$ and $A$ is $Z$-dependent, so is $B$. By construction, $B$ is primitive. A nonzero base polynomial of degree $\deg(H)$ vanishes formally on at most $\deg(H)$ affine lines. On every other target line,

$$H(\ell_L(t))B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0$$

and $H(\ell_L(t))\ne 0$. Cancellation in the domain $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ therefore gives $B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
View $A$ as a polynomial in $Z$, let $H\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ be the greatest common divisor of its $Z$-coefficients, and write $A=HB$ with $B$ primitive. Then $B$ is squarefree and $Z$-dependent, $\deg(H)\le D$, at most $\deg(H)$ target lines $L\in T$ satisfy $H(\ell_L(t))\equiv 0$, and

$$B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0$$

for every other target line $L\in T$.
lemmas.title: Primitive content removal

lemmas.proof_markdown: Suppose an irreducible factor $C$ divided both $B$ and $B_Z$. Squarefreeness of $B$ forces $C_Z=0$. Since $\deg_Z(C)\le\deg_Z(B)<p$, this makes $C$ independent of $Z$. Such a factor would divide every $Z$-coefficient of $B$, contradicting primitivity. Hence $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $d$ be positive, and let $B\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ be primitive, squarefree, and $Z$-dependent, with $(1,1,d)$-weighted degree at most $D<p$. Then

$$\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$
lemmas.title: Vertical separability

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The coprime graph-line bound recorded in P0, applied to $B$ and $B_Z$, bounds the graph lines on which both vanish formally by $D(D-1)$. Together with the at most $D$ content lines, these deletions have normalized mass at most

$$\frac{D^2}{p(p+1)}\le\left(\frac Dp\right)^2.$$

On every other target line, $B_Z(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D-d$. Its zero incidences therefore have normalized mass at most

$$\frac{D-d}{p}\le\frac Dp.$$

Every retained edge is accepted and lies on a graph on which $B$ vanishes formally, so it satisfies the two asserted pointwise conditions.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be the structured certificate graph, and let $A=HB$ be as in P5, with $B$ satisfying P6. Delete every edge on a content line, every edge on a line $L$ for which

$$B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0\qquad\text{and}\qquad B_Z(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv 0,$$

and every remaining edge $(x,L)$ for which $B_Z(x_1,x_2,f(x))=0$, where $x=(x_1,x_2)$. If $E_{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the retained edge set, then

$$\frac{|E\setminus E_{\mathrm{cl}}|}{p^2(p+1)}\le\left(\frac Dp\right)^2+\frac Dp,$$

and every $(x,L)\in E_{\mathrm{cl}}$ satisfies

$$B(x_1,x_2,f(x))=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad B_Z(x_1,x_2,f(x))\ne 0.$$
lemmas.title: Vertical cleanup

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Charge each removed edge when its first endpoint is deleted. Point-vertex deletions cost less than $D/(p+1)$ in normalized mass, while line-vertex deletions cost at most $D/p$. Thus peeling costs less than $2D/p$. Including the cleanup cost from P7, the total deleted mass is less than

$$\left(\frac Dp\right)^2+3\frac Dp<\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2},$$

where the last inequality is P2. The original certificate has normalized edge mass at least $a_\theta\varepsilon$, so the remaining graph has normalized edge mass at least $a_\theta\varepsilon/2$. In particular it is nonempty, and termination gives degree greater than $D$ at every remaining vertex.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Starting from the cleaned graph with edge set $E_{\mathrm{cl}}$, repeatedly delete any current point or line vertex of degree at most $D$, together with its incident edges. The resulting graph $G_1$ is nonempty, every vertex $v\in V(G_1)$ satisfies $\deg_{G_1}(v)>D$, and

$$\frac{|E(G_1)|}{p^2(p+1)}\ge\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2}.$$
lemmas.title: High-degree core

lemmas.proof_markdown: Choose a point vertex $b$ in a connected component $\Gamma$. More than $D$ distinct incident line vertices meet the simple root $(b,f(b))$. The simple-root lifting fact recorded in P0, namely KTZ Lemma 6.1, supplies a polynomial $Q_\Gamma$ of total degree at most $d$ with $B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma)\equiv 0$ and with the required label identity on every line incident to $b$. The propagation fact recorded in P0, namely KTZ Lemma 6.3, propagates these identities along every edge of the connected component. Acceptedness then gives $Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
For every connected component $\Gamma$ of $G_1$, there exists $Q_\Gamma\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv 0,$$

$$Q_\Gamma(\ell_L(t))\equiv P_L(t)\qquad\text{for every line vertex }L\text{ of }\Gamma,$$

and

$$Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)\qquad\text{for every point vertex }x\text{ of }\Gamma.$$
lemmas.title: Component polynomial template

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Evaluation at $Z=Q_\Gamma$ defines a homomorphism whose kernel is generated by $Z-Q_\Gamma$. Since $B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma)=0$, it follows that $Z-Q_\Gamma$ divides $B$. Distinct polynomials $Q_\Gamma$ yield distinct monic irreducible factors. Consequently their number is at most $\deg_Z(B)$. The weighted-degree and structured-branch bounds give

$$\deg_Z(B)\le\frac{\operatorname{wdeg}(B)}{d}\le\frac Dd\le K_\theta.$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let

$$\mathcal{Q}=\{Q_\Gamma:\Gamma\text{ is a connected component of }G_1\}.$$

Then every $Q_\Gamma\in\mathcal{Q}$ satisfies $Z-Q_\Gamma\mid B$, and

$$|\mathcal{Q}|\le\deg_Z(B)\le\frac{\operatorname{wdeg}(B)}{d}\le\frac Dd\le K_\theta.$$
lemmas.title: Template compression

lemmas.proof_markdown: Partition the edges of $G_1$ according to their component template. The graph has normalized edge mass at least $a_\theta\varepsilon/2$, and P10 gives at most $K_\theta$ distinct templates. Hence one template $Q$ carries normalized edge mass at least $a_\theta\varepsilon/(2K_\theta)$. By P9, this $Q$ equals $f$ at every supporting point. Since a point lies on at most $p+1$ affine lines, the density of those supporting points is at least the normalized edge mass.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
There exists $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2K_\theta}.$$
lemmas.title: Single-template agreement

lemmas.proof_markdown: The direct alternative in $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$ gives agreement at least $c_\theta\varepsilon$. In the structured alternative, P11 gives agreement at least $a_\theta\varepsilon/(2K_\theta)$. Taking the smaller of these two constants proves the conclusion.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Fix $0<\theta\le 1/4$ and suppose $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$ holds with constants $C_\theta,K_\theta,a_\theta,c_\theta$ as in P1. For every prime $p$, every integer $d$ with $100<d<p$, every function $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$, and every supplied degree-at-most-$d$ line table whose acceptance satisfies $\varepsilon\ge C_\theta(d/p)^{1-\theta}$,

$$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\min\left\{c_\theta,\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\right\}\varepsilon.$$
lemmas.title: Conditional fixed-parameter decoder

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix $\eta>0$ and choose $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $0<d/p<1$ and $\eta\ge\theta$,

$$\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}\ge\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\theta}.$$

Thus the trigger with exponent $1-\eta$ implies the trigger required by P12 for this value of $\theta$. Renaming the constants from P12 gives $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ and the stated conclusion.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Assume $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$ holds for every $\theta$ with $0<\theta\le 1/4$. Then, for every fixed $\eta>0$, there exist constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $d$ with $100<d<p$, every function $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$, and every supplied degree-at-most-$d$ line table,

$$\varepsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$

implies

$$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\eta\varepsilon.$$
lemmas.title: Fixed-exponent closure

lemmas.proof_markdown: Iteratively delete every point vertex and line vertex whose current carrier degree is below $k_0$. All point-side deletions remove at most $p^2k_0$ edges, and all line-side deletions remove at most $p(p+1)k_0$ edges. After normalization by the $p^2(p+1)$ incidences, the loss is at most $$\frac{k_0}{p+1}+\frac{k_0}{p}<\frac{\delta}{50}.$$ Hence the surviving edge mass exceeds $\delta-\delta/50$ and is, in particular, at least $\delta/4$. Every surviving vertex has degree at least $k_0$. Its line set is contained in the original line support, so $\lambda\le\sigma$; since every line has at most $p$ incident edges, its normalized line measure is at least its normalized edge mass, giving $\lambda\ge\delta/4$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, and let $G$ be an accepted-carrier subgraph of the affine point-line incidence graph of $\mathbb F_p^2$ with normalized edge mass $\delta>0$ and line support at most $\sigma$, where $0<\delta\le\sigma\le1$. Put $k_0=\lfloor\delta p/100\rfloor$. There is a subgraph $G_0\subseteq G$ with minimum degree at least $k_0$, normalized edge mass at least $\delta/4$, and normalized line measure $\lambda$ satisfying $\delta/4\le\lambda\le\sigma$.
lemmas.title: Carrier pruning

lemmas.proof_markdown: The hypotheses $\sigma\ge\delta$ and $\delta^3\ge10^{15}d\sigma/p$ imply $$\delta^2\ge\frac{10^{15}d}{p},\qquad \delta p\ge\sqrt{10^{15}dp}>3\cdot10^9,$$ and therefore $k_0\ge\delta p/200$. Select every line of $\mathcal L_0$ independently with probability $\theta=8/k_0$. For a fixed $L\in\mathcal L_0$ and a point-neighbor $x$ of $L$, at least $k_0-1$ other retained lines pass through $x$. Thus the probability that $x$ is not covered is at most $(1-\theta)^{k_0-1}$, and its coverage probability exceeds $3/4$. The coverage indicators at distinct neighbors of $L$ depend on disjoint sets of other lines. Hoeffding's inequality therefore bounds the probability that fewer than half of the neighbors are covered by $\exp(-k_0/8)$. Since $k_0\ge8\log(4p(p+1))$, a union bound over the $p(p+1)$ affine lines gives total coverage-failure probability below $1/4$. If $r=|R|$, then $$\mathbb E[r]=\theta|\mathcal L_0|\ge200(p+1),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(r)\le\mathbb E[r].$$ Chebyshev's inequality gives, with failure probability below $1/4$, $$\frac12\mathbb E[r]\le r\le2\mathbb E[r].$$ Consequently, some deterministic selection satisfies the coverage property and $$100(p+1)\le r\le\frac{16|\mathcal L_0|}{k_0}\le\frac{6400\sigma p}{\delta}.$$ These estimates incur only constant failure probability and no additional power of $\delta$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let $G_0$ have the properties in P1 with line set $\mathcal L_0$. Assume $\delta^3\ge10^{15}d\sigma/p$. There is a set $R\subseteq\mathcal L_0$ such that every $L\in\mathcal L_0$ has at least half of its point-neighbors in $G_0$ also incident in $G_0$ to a line in $R\setminus\{L\}$ and, for $r=|R|$, $$100(p+1)\le r\le\frac{6400\sigma p}{\delta}.$$
lemmas.title: Support-sensitive selector

lemmas.proof_markdown: Let $V_D$ be the space of polynomials of weighted degree at most $D$. The definition of $D$ gives $D^2>256dr$, and the weighted monomial count gives $$\dim(V_D)\ge\frac{D^3}{64d}>r(D+1).$$ Since $\deg(P_L)\le d$, the substitution $A(L(t),P_L(t))$ has degree at most $D$. Each selected line therefore imposes at most $D+1$ homogeneous linear conditions on the coefficients of $A$. There are fewer conditions than unknowns, so a nonzero interpolant exists. From P2, $$D\le1280\sqrt{\frac{d\sigma p}{\delta}}+16\le\frac{1280\delta p}{\sqrt{10^{15}}}+16<\frac{\delta p}{10000}.$$ Hence $D<p$, $D<k_0/2$, and $D<k_1/2$. Also, $r>D$. If an interpolant were independent of $Z$, it would be a nonzero bivariate polynomial of degree at most $D$ vanishing identically on more than $D$ affine lines, which is impossible because each such line contributes a distinct linear factor. Thus $A_Z\not\equiv0$. Choose an interpolant of minimum weighted degree. If it has a repeated irreducible factor, replacing it by the product of its distinct irreducible factors preserves every graph identity in the integral domains $\mathbb F_p[t]$ and lowers its weighted degree. Minimality therefore permits $A$ to be chosen squarefree.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses and notation of P2, assign weights $\operatorname{wt}(X)=\operatorname{wt}(Y)=1$ and $\operatorname{wt}(Z)=d$, set $k_1=\lfloor\delta p/1000\rfloor$, and put $$D=16\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{dr}\right\rfloor+1\right).$$ For line labels $P_L$ of degree at most $d$, there is a nonzero squarefree polynomial $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree at most $D$, with $A_Z\not\equiv0$, such that $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ for every $L\in R$. Moreover, $$D\le1280\sqrt{\frac{d\sigma p}{\delta}}+16<\frac{\delta p}{10000},$$ so $D<p$, $D<k_0/2$, $D<k_1/2$, and $r>D$.
lemmas.title: Weighted interpolation

lemmas.proof_markdown: Fix $L\in\mathcal L_0$. By the selector property, at least $k_0/2>D$ distinct accepted points of $L$ also lie on selected retained lines. At every such point $x$, the two accepted labels have the common value $$P_L(x)=f(x)=P_{L'}(x).$$ Since $A(L'(t),P_{L'}(t))\equiv0$ on the selected line $L'$, it follows that $A(x,P_L(x))=0$. The polynomial $A(L(t),P_L(t))$ has degree at most $D$ and more than $D$ distinct roots, so it vanishes identically. Write $A=HB$, where $H$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. If $H$ vanishes identically on an affine line, that line's defining linear polynomial divides $H$; hence at most $\deg(H)\le D$ affine lines are content lines. On every other retained line, $$H(L(t))B(L(t),P_L(t))=0$$ in the integral domain $\mathbb F_p[t]$. Since $H(L(t))$ is not the zero polynomial, $$B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$ This is an integral-domain inference, not pointwise division by $H$, and the root count uses distinct points rather than multiplicity.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $A$, $D$, $G_0$, $\mathcal L_0$, and $R$ satisfy P2 and P3. Then $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ for every $L\in\mathcal L_0$. Write $A=H(X,Y)B(X,Y,Z)$, where $H$ is the greatest common divisor in $\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of the coefficients of $A$ as a polynomial in $Z$, and $B$ is primitive in $Z$. The polynomial $B$ is squarefree and has total degree at most $D<p$. At most $D$ lines in $\mathcal L_0$ satisfy $H(L(t))\equiv0$, and every other $L\in\mathcal L_0$ satisfies $$B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$
lemmas.title: Coefficient-content removal

lemmas.proof_markdown: Factor $B$ in $\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ as $$B=c\prod_i P_i,$$ where $c\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ and the $P_i$ are distinct irreducibles. If some $P_i$ were independent of $Z$, it would divide every coefficient of $B$ as a polynomial in $Z$, contradicting primitivity. Thus every $P_i$ has positive $Z$-degree. Since $\deg_Z(P_i)<p$, its derivative $(P_i)_Z$ is nonzero in characteristic $p$. Its smaller $Z$-degree also implies that $P_i$ does not divide $(P_i)_Z$. Reducing the product rule modulo $P_i$ gives $$B_Z\equiv c(P_i)_Z\prod_{j\ne i}P_j\not\equiv0\pmod{P_i}.$$ Hence no irreducible factor of $B$ divides $B_Z$, and $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. The argument uses neither absolute irreducibility nor factorization over an algebraic closure.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime. If $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ is squarefree, primitive as a polynomial in $Z$, and satisfies $\deg(B)<p$, then $$\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$
lemmas.title: Vertical derivative coprimality

lemmas.proof_markdown: Apply the resultant line bound to the coprime pair $(B,B_Z)$. There are at most $D$ content lines and at most $D(D-1)$ further lines on which the graph identities for $B$ and $B_Z$ degenerate simultaneously. On every remaining line, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$ and therefore has at most $D$ roots. The resulting normalized edge loss is at most $$\frac{D}{p(p+1)}+\frac{D(D-1)}{p(p+1)}+\frac{D}{p}<\frac{\delta}{16},$$ using $D<\delta p/10000$. Iteratively deleting point and line vertices of current degree below $k_1$ costs at most $$\frac{k_1}{p+1}+\frac{k_1}{p}<\frac{\delta}{500}.$$ Starting from edge mass at least $\delta/4$, the surviving graph therefore has edge mass at least $\delta/8$ and minimum degree at least $k_1$. Every surviving incidence is accepted and avoids the zero set of $B_Z$, so $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$ at every surviving point. No discriminant or Markov inequality is used.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let the retained graph and polynomial $B$ satisfy P4 and P5. Assume that its normalized edge mass before degeneracy deletion is at least $\delta/4$, that $D<\delta p/10000$, and set $k_1=\lfloor\delta p/1000\rfloor$. Deleting the content lines, resultant-degenerate lines, and incidences at which $B_Z$ vanishes, followed by pruning all vertices of degree below $k_1$, produces a graph $G_1$ with normalized edge mass at least $\delta/8$, minimum degree at least $k_1$, and $$B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$$ at every surviving point $x$. The pre-pruning deletion has normalized mass below $\delta/16$, and the final pruning has normalized cost below $\delta/500$.
lemmas.title: Degenerate-root deletion

lemmas.proof_markdown: Fix a surviving point, translate its base coordinates to $(0,0)$, and put $\alpha=f(0,0)$. Construct $$\Phi=\alpha+\Phi_1+\Phi_2+\cdots\in\mathbb F_p[[X,Y]],$$ with each $\Phi_j$ homogeneous of degree $j$. At stage $j$, the degree-$j$ residual in $B(X,Y,\Phi)$ depends linearly on $\Phi_j$ with coefficient $B_Z(0,0,\alpha)$. Since this coefficient is nonzero, the residual is canceled uniquely by dividing by that scalar. No factorial or higher-derivative denominator is inverted. Restricting $\Phi$ to any surviving incident line gives the unique formal root with constant term $\alpha$. The corresponding line polynomial is another such root and has degree at most $d$, so the two restrictions coincide. More than $D$ distinct incident directions survive because $k_1>D$. Hence, for every $d<j\le D$, the homogeneous polynomial $\Phi_j$ vanishes on more than $D\ge j$ projective directions and must be zero. Let $$Q=\alpha+\Phi_1+\cdots+\Phi_d.$$ Substituting a polynomial of total degree at most $d$ into a polynomial of weighted degree at most $D$ gives $\deg B(X,Y,Q)\le D$. Its homogeneous terms through degree $D$ vanish by the construction, so $$B(X,Y,Q)\equiv0.$$ At a surviving edge, simple-root uniqueness identifies the restriction of $Q$ with the incident line label. Repeating across adjacent point and line vertices propagates the same $Q$ throughout the connected component, where every accepted point satisfies $Q(x)=f(x)$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $C$ be a connected component of $G_1$. Suppose every line vertex $L$ of $C$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, every point vertex $x$ satisfies $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$, every line label has degree at most $d$, and the minimum degree is $k_1>D$. Then there is a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0$$ and $$Q(x)=f(x)$$ for every point vertex $x$ of $C$.
lemmas.title: Simple-root propagation

lemmas.proof_markdown: Minimum degree gives $$e\ge\frac{\kappa a}{2},\qquad e\ge\kappa b,$$ while point-line incidence mixing gives $$e\le ab+u\sqrt{ab}.$$ The theorem hypothesis and $d\ge101$ imply $$u<\frac{\delta}{8000}\le\frac{\kappa}{4}.$$ If $a<\kappa/4$, then $e\ge\kappa b$ and the mixing upper bound imply $3b\le\sqrt{ab}$ and hence $9b\le a$. It follows that $$e\le\frac{a^2}{9}+\frac{ua}{3}<\frac{\kappa a}{9},$$ contradicting $e\ge\kappa a/2$. If $b<\kappa/4$, then $e\ge\kappa a/2$ and the mixing upper bound imply $a\le\sqrt{ab}$ and hence $a\le b$. Therefore $$e\le b^2+ub<\frac{\kappa b}{2},$$ contradicting $e\ge\kappa b$. Thus $a,b\ge\kappa/4\ge\delta/8000$. By P7, the component's polynomial agrees with $f$ on all of its point vertices, so its global agreement is at least $a\ge\delta/8000$. The term $u=1/\sqrt{p+1}$ is the sole incidence Cauchy–Schwarz loss.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Assume $\delta^3\ge10^{15}d\sigma/p$, and let $C$ be a nonempty connected component of $G_1$. Define its normalized point, line, and edge measures by $$a=\frac{|V_{\mathrm{pt}}(C)|}{p^2},\qquad b=\frac{|V_{\mathrm{ln}}(C)|}{p(p+1)},\qquad e=\frac{|E(C)|}{p^2(p+1)},$$ and put $\kappa=k_1/p$ and $u=1/\sqrt{p+1}$. Then $$a,b\ge\frac{\kappa}{4}\ge\frac{\delta}{8000}.$$ Consequently, the polynomial supplied by P7 satisfies $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{\delta}{8000}.$$
lemmas.title: Component mixing

lemmas.proof_markdown: Substituting the selector size into the interpolation degree gives $$D=O\left(\sqrt{\frac{d\sigma p}{\delta}}\right).$$ Comparing this with $D=O(\delta p)$ and squaring yields $$\frac{d\sigma p}{\delta}=O(\delta^2p^2),$$ which is equivalent to $$\delta^3=\Omega\left(\frac{d\sigma}{p}\right).$$ The linear root budget $D=O(\delta p)$ is required independently by identity extension, the $D/p$ bad-incidence deletion, and simple-root lifting. By contrast, requiring only the resultant contribution $D^2/p^2$ to be at most order $\delta$ gives the weaker condition $\delta^2=\Omega(d\sigma/p)$. Incidence mixing requires only $\delta=\Omega(p^{-1/2})$, also weaker in the stated regime. Setting $\sigma=1$ recovers the cubic threshold $\delta=\Omega((d/p)^{1/3})$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p,d,\delta,\sigma,r,D>0$ satisfy $$r=O\left(\frac{\sigma p}{\delta}\right),\qquad D=\Theta(\sqrt{dr}).$$ If the later stages impose $D=O(\delta p)$, then the resulting closure condition is $$\delta^3=\Omega\left(\frac{d\sigma}{p}\right).$$
lemmas.title: Cubic scale ledger

lemmas.proof_markdown: Under $\sigma\le A\delta$, $$10^{15}\frac{d\sigma}{p}\le10^{15}\frac{Ad\delta}{p}.$$ Thus $\delta^2\ge10^{15}Ad/p$ implies $\delta^3\ge10^{15}d\sigma/p$, producing a square-root threshold in $d/p$. Every carrier also satisfies $\sigma\ge\delta$. Hence even the smallest possible support scale within this balance is of order $\delta$, so the support-sensitive interpolation relation cannot yield an exponent exceeding $1/2$. Because $\sigma\le A\delta$ is an additional structural hypothesis and diffuse carriers may have much larger support, this is not an unconditional benchmark improvement.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $A>0$ and $0<\delta\le\sigma\le1$, and suppose $\sigma\le A\delta$. If $$\delta^2\ge10^{15}\frac{Ad}{p},$$ then $$\delta^3\ge10^{15}\frac{d\sigma}{p}.$$
lemmas.title: Concentrated-carrier threshold

lemmas.proof_markdown: Fix an affine line $L$. Its $p$ values are independent and uniform in $\mathbb F_p$. For $a\in\mathbb F_p$, let $$N_a=|\{x\in L:f(x)=a\}|,\qquad Y=\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_p}\mathbf 1_{\{N_a=r\}}.$$ For a fixed $a$, $$q:=\Pr[N_a=r]=\binom prp^{-r}\left(1-\frac1p\right)^{p-r}.$$ Since $r^2\le p$, $\binom prp^{-r}\ge1/(2r!)$, while $(1-1/p)^{p-r}\ge(1-1/p)^p\ge1/4$. Hence $q\ge1/(8r!)$. Moreover, $r!\le r^r\le p^{1/4}$, so $$\mu:=\mathbb E[Y]=pq\ge\frac{p^{3/4}}8\ge1.$$ For distinct $a,b\in\mathbb F_p$, $$\Pr[N_a=N_b=r]=\frac{p!}{r!r!(p-2r)!}p^{-2r}\left(1-\frac2p\right)^{p-2r}\le\frac1{(r!)^2}\le64q^2.$$ Consequently, $$\mathbb E[Y^2]\le\mu+64\mu^2\le65\mu^2.$$ Cauchy–Schwarz gives $$\Pr[Y>0]\ge\frac{\mathbb E[Y]^2}{\mathbb E[Y^2]}\ge\frac1{65}.$$ On $\{Y>0\}$, one has $M_L\ge r$, so $\mathbb E[M_L]\ge r/65$. Assigning each line a constant label equal to one of its modal values gives agreement $M_L/p$ on that line. Averaging over lines and using linearity of expectation yields $\mathbb E[A]\ge r/(65p)$; no independence between distinct lines is asserted.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p\ge\lceil e^{32}\rceil$ be prime and set $$r=\left\lfloor\frac{\log p}{4\log\log p}\right\rfloor.$$ Choose $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$ independently and uniformly at every point. For every affine line $L$, define $$M_L=\max_{a\in\mathbb F_p}|\{x\in L:f(x)=a\}|,$$ and define the modal local agreement by $$A=\frac1{p(p+1)}\sum_L\frac{M_L}{p}.$$ Then, for every $L$, $$\mathbb E[M_L]\ge\frac r{65},\qquad \mathbb E[A]\ge\frac{r}{65p}.$$
lemmas.title: Modal occupancy lower bound

lemmas.proof_markdown: For a fixed line $L$ and every positive integer $s$, the factorial-moment bound gives $$\Pr[N_a\ge s]\le\mathbb E\binom{N_a}{s}=\binom psp^{-s}\le\frac1{s!}.$$ A union bound over the $p$ values and $s!\ge(s/e)^s$ yield $$\Pr[M_L\ge s]\le\frac p{s!}\le p\left(\frac es\right)^s.$$ For $s_0=\lceil4\log p/\log\log p\rceil$, the resulting tail satisfies $$\sum_{s>s_0}p\left(\frac es\right)^s<1.$$ Therefore $$\mathbb E[M_L]\le s_0+1\le25r,$$ and averaging $M_L/p$ over the lines gives $\mathbb E[A]\le25r/p$. Changing one point value affects only the $p+1$ incident lines and changes each affected modal multiplicity by at most $1$. Since $A$ is normalized by $p^2(p+1)$ incidences, every one of the $p^2$ independent point values has bounded difference at most $1/p^2$. McDiarmid's inequality consequently gives $$\Pr\left[A-\mathbb E[A]\ge\frac{25r}{p}\right]\le\exp\left(-\frac{2(25r/p)^2}{p^2(1/p^2)^2}\right)=e^{-1250r^2}.$$ Using $\mathbb E[A]\le25r/p$ and the stated lower bound on $p$ proves $$\Pr\left[A>\frac{50r}{p}\right]\le e^{-1250r^2}\le\frac{r}{520p}.$$ No Markov inequality is used.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p\ge\lceil e^{32}\rceil$ be prime, let $r=\lfloor\log p/(4\log\log p)\rfloor$, and let $f$, $M_L$, and $A$ be defined as in P11. Put $s_0=\lceil4\log p/\log\log p\rceil$. Then, for every affine line $L$, $$\mathbb E[M_L]\le s_0+1\le25r,$$ and $$\mathbb E[A]\le\frac{25r}{p},\qquad \Pr\left[A>\frac{50r}{p}\right]\le e^{-1250r^2}\le\frac{r}{520p}.$$
lemmas.title: Modal concentration

lemmas.proof_markdown: Choose $f$ randomly as in P11 and give every affine line a modal constant label. Let $A$ be the resulting local agreement. For a fixed polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $101$, the count $$Z_Q=|\{x\in\mathbb F_p^2:Q(x)=f(x)\}|$$ has distribution $\operatorname{Bin}(p^2,1/p)$ and mean $p$. Chernoff's inequality gives $$\Pr[Z_Q\ge2p]\le\left(\frac e4\right)^p.$$ The polynomial space has dimension $N=5253$ and therefore contains $p^N$ formal polynomials. If $G$ is the event that every such polynomial has normalized agreement below $2/p$, a union bound gives $$\Pr[G^c]\le p^N\left(\frac e4\right)^p\le e^{-p/4}\le\frac{r}{520p}.$$ Let $H=\{A\le50r/p\}$. By P12, $\Pr[H^c]\le r/(520p)$. Since $0\le A\le1$, P11 and these exceptional-probability bounds imply $$\mathbb E[A\mathbf 1_{G\cap H}]\ge\frac{r}{65p}-\frac{r}{520p}-\frac{r}{520p}>\frac{r}{130p}.$$ Some deterministic outcome therefore belongs to $G\cap H$ and has $A>r/(130p)$. Taking $\varepsilon=A$ gives all the asserted bounds. Every modal label is constant and hence has degree at most $101$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $d=101$, let $N=(d+1)(d+2)/2=5253$, and let $p\ge\max\{\lceil e^{32}\rceil,100N^2\}$ be prime. Put $r=\lfloor\log p/(4\log\log p)\rfloor$. There exist a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$ and constant affine-line labels $P_L$ such that, with $$\varepsilon=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)],$$ one has $$\frac{r}{130p}\le\varepsilon\le\frac{50r}{p}$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_{101}(f):=\max_{\substack{Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\ \deg Q\le101}}\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]<\frac2p.$$
lemmas.title: Deterministic modal table

lemmas.proof_markdown: Let $C,c>0$ be arbitrary. Fix the legal ambient degree $d=101$ and choose a sufficiently large prime $p$ for which $$r=\left\lfloor\frac{\log p}{4\log\log p}\right\rfloor>\max\left\{130\cdot101C,\frac{260}{c}\right\}.$$ P13 supplies a point table and legal constant labels satisfying $$\frac{r}{130p}\le\varepsilon\le\frac{50r}{p},\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_{101}(f)<\frac2p.$$ Thus $$\varepsilon>C\frac{101}{p}=C\frac d p,$$ whereas $$\operatorname{Agr}_{101}(f)<\frac2p<\frac{cr}{130p}\le c\varepsilon.$$ This contradicts the claimed implication for every fixed pair $C,c>0$. On the other hand, for every fixed $\eta>0$, $$\frac{\varepsilon}{(101/p)^{1-\eta}}\le\frac{50r}{101^{1-\eta}p^\eta}\longrightarrow0,$$ since $r=O(\log p/\log\log p)=o(p^\eta)$. Hence this construction remains below every fixed-$\eta$ trigger of scale $(101/p)^{1-\eta}$ and does not refute such a statement.
lemmas.statement_markdown: There exist absolute constants $C,c>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $d$ with $101\le d<p$, every function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and every family of affine-line labels of degree at most $d$, the implication $$\varepsilon\ge C\frac d p\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c\varepsilon$$ holds, where $\varepsilon=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\substack{Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\ \deg Q\le d}}\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)].$$
lemmas.title: Exact-linear soundness

lemmas.proof_markdown: Since $d<p$, choose distinct elements $a_0,\ldots,a_d$ and $b_0,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathbb F_p$, and put $$S=\{(a_i,b_j):i+j\le d\}.$$ For every $i+j\le d$, define $$N_{i,j}(X,Y)=\prod_{h<i}(X-a_h)\prod_{k<j}(Y-b_k).$$ These polynomials have total degree at most $d$. Their evaluations on $S$ form a triangular matrix with nonzero diagonal, because $N_{i,j}(a_u,b_v)=0$ when $u<i$ or $v<j$, while $$N_{i,j}(a_i,b_j)=\prod_{h<i}(a_i-a_h)\prod_{k<j}(b_j-b_k)\ne0.$$ They therefore form an evaluation basis on $S$, so the arbitrary values of $f|_S$ extend to a polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $d$. Since $$|S|=\frac{(d+1)(d+2)}2,$$ the normalized agreement is at least $|S|/p^2$. At $d=p-1$, this equals $(p+1)/(2p)>1/2$; at $d=101$ and $p=103$, it equals $5253/10609$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: For every prime $p$, every integer $d$ with $101\le d<p$, and every function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{(d+1)(d+2)}{2p^2}.$$
lemmas.title: Triangular information set

lemmas.proof_markdown: For every affine line $L$, fix a parametrization $\ell_L:\mathbb F_p\to L$, choose $d$ distinct parameters $t_{L,1},\ldots,t_{L,d}$, and define $$P_L(t)=\prod_{i=1}^d(t-t_{L,i}).$$ Because $d<p$, this polynomial has degree exactly $d$ and precisely $d$ distinct roots. With $f=0$, exactly $d$ of the $p$ incidences on every line are accepted. Hence $\varepsilon=d/p$, and every line supports an accepted incidence, so $\sigma=1$. The total-degree-zero polynomial $Q=0$ agrees with $f$ everywhere, giving $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=1$. In particular, fixing $d=101$ and letting $p$ grow through the primes gives $\sigma/\varepsilon=p/101\to\infty$, so no uniform relation $\sigma=O(\varepsilon)$ follows from local acceptance. The example is harmless for soundness because it already has perfect global agreement.
lemmas.statement_markdown: For every prime $p$ and every integer $d$ with $101\le d<p$, there exist a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$ and degree-$d$ affine-line labels such that their local agreement and line-support parameters satisfy $$\varepsilon=\frac d p,\qquad \sigma=1,$$ while $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=1.$$
lemmas.title: Diffuse accepted support

lemmas.proof_markdown: For each $i$, choose a nonzero vector $v_i\in\ker(\ell_i)$. On a line parametrized by $a+tv_i$, the coefficient of $t^{d+1}$ in $f(a+tv_i)$ is $$f(v_i)=\prod_{j=1}^{d+1}\ell_j(v_i)=0.$$ Thus the restriction has degree at most $d$ and is a legal label. The corresponding classes comprise $d+1$ of the $p+1$ projective directions and contribute exactly $(d+1)/(p+1)$ to normalized local agreement. However, the total-degree-zero polynomial $Q=0$ agrees with $f$ on $$\bigcup_{i=1}^{d+1}\ker(\ell_i).$$ These are distinct lines through the origin, whose union has size $1+(d+1)(p-1)$. Consequently, $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]=\frac{1+(d+1)(p-1)}{p^2}=\Theta\left(\frac d p\right).$$ The construction therefore already contains a global polynomial matching the local scale, so the asserted lack of such a polynomial is false.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ range over primes, let $101\le d<p$, let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{d+1}\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ be pairwise nonproportional nonzero homogeneous linear forms, and set $f=\prod_{i=1}^{d+1}\ell_i$. Label every affine line in direction $\ker(\ell_i)$ by the restriction of $f$, and use labels of degree at most $d$ on all remaining lines. The $d+1$ specified direction classes contribute normalized local agreement $(d+1)/(p+1)$, while no polynomial of total degree at most $d$ agrees with $f$ on a $\Theta(d/p)$ fraction of $\mathbb F_p^2$.
lemmas.title: Concentrated direction classes

lemmas.proof_markdown: Because $p$ is odd, $$B=(Z-X)(Z+X)$$ has distinct factors and is squarefree. Both branches have total degree $1\le d$ and satisfy $$B(X,Y,Q_+(X,Y))=B(X,Y,Q_-(X,Y))=0.$$ At the origin, $$Q_+(0,0)=Q_-(0,0)=0,$$ while $$B_Z=2Z,\qquad B_Z(0,0,0)=0.$$ The branches are nevertheless distinct. Thus the common incidence is compatible with both branches and cannot select one for propagation; vertical-simple-root deletion is logically necessary for this propagation argument.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $101\le d<p$. For $$B=Z^2-X^2,\qquad Q_+=X,\qquad Q_-=-X,$$ the common incidence $Q_+(0,0)=Q_-(0,0)=0$ uniquely determines which total-degree-at-most-$d$ branch propagates through the origin without assuming $B_Z(0,0,0)\ne0$.
lemmas.title: Branch collision

lemmas.proof_markdown: Write $$B(X,Y,Z)=\sum_{e\ge0}b_e(X,Y)Z^e.$$ If $B_Z=0$, then $e\,b_e(X,Y)=0$ in $\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ whenever $e>0$. Hence every positive $Z$-exponent occurring in $B$ must be divisible by $p$. On the other hand, every monomial $X^aY^bZ^e$ in the weighted-degree space satisfies $$a+b+de\le D<p.$$ Every possible positive exponent therefore satisfies $0<e<p$ and cannot be divisible by $p$. Thus $b_e=0$ for every $e>0$, so $B$ is independent of $Z$. In particular, an expression such as $Z^p-G(X,Y)$ has weighted degree at least $dp>D$ and lies outside the interpolation space. Hence inseparability is not active under the cutoff $D<p$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let $D<p$. Under the weights $$\operatorname{wt}(X)=\operatorname{wt}(Y)=1,\qquad \operatorname{wt}(Z)=d,$$ there exists a polynomial $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of positive $Z$-degree and weighted degree at most $D$ such that $$B_Z=0.$$
lemmas.title: Vertical inseparability

lemmas.proof_markdown:
KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives the affine point–line mixing inequality with normalized error

$$
\frac{\sqrt{\mu(X)\tau}}{\sqrt{p+1}}.
$$

The first numerical hypothesis and $d>100$ imply

$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{p+1}}\le \frac{k}{4p}.
$$

Applying the minimum-degree argument of KTZ Lemma 6.2 to the point and line sides of $G$ therefore gives

$$
\mu(X),\tau\ge \frac{k}{4p}.
$$

Since $t=\tau p(p+1)$, the line-side estimate also gives $t\ge k(p+1)/4$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime and let $d$ be an integer satisfying $100<d<p$. Let $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$, and assign to every affine line $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^2$ a polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most $d$. Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a connected subgraph of the accepted-incidence graph with minimum degree $k$, where an incidence $(x,L)$ is accepted when $P_L(x)=f(x)$. Put

$$
t=|T|,\qquad \mu(X)=\frac{|X|}{p^2},\qquad \tau=\frac{t}{p(p+1)},\qquad C_*=2^{40}.
$$

Assume

$$
k^2\ge C_*dp,\qquad k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2.
$$

Then

$$
\mu(X)\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.
$$

In particular, $t\ge k(p+1)/4$.
lemmas.title: Component Measures

dependencies: uniqueness of the affine line through two points
lemmas.proof_markdown:
Select every line of $T$ independently with probability $8/k$. For a fixed $L\in T$ and $x\in N_G(L)$, at least $k-1$ other accepted lines of $G$ pass through $x$. Thus $x$ is reached with probability at least

$$
1-\left(1-\frac{8}{k}\right)^{k-1}\ge\frac34.
$$

For distinct points of $L$, the relevant sets of other lines are disjoint, because two distinct points have only one common affine line, namely $L$. Their reach indicators are therefore independent. A Chernoff bound gives

$$
\Pr\left[\text{at most half of }N_G(L)\text{ is reached}\right]
 \le e^{-\deg_G(L)/24}
 \le e^{-k/24}.
$$

The numerical hypotheses imply $k\gg\log p$, so a union bound over fewer than $2p^2$ affine lines succeeds. A second Chernoff bound simultaneously places the sample size between half and twice its expectation $8t/k$. Hence a deterministic choice of $R$ has the asserted coverage and size. By P1,

$$
|R|\ge\frac{4t}{k}\ge p+1.
$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1, there exists a set $R\subseteq T$ such that

$$
\frac{4t}{k}\le |R|\le\frac{16t}{k},
$$

and, for every $L\in T$,

$$
\left|\left\{x\in N_G(L):\exists\,M\in R\setminus\{L\}\text{ with }(x,M)\in E\right\}\right|
>\frac12\deg_G(L).
$$

Moreover, $|R|\ge p+1$ and $|R|=\Theta(\tau p^2/k)$ with absolute implied constants.
lemmas.title: Reaching Family

lemmas.proof_markdown:
From the definition of $D$ and the bounds on $r$ supplied by P2,

$$
D^2>256dr,
$$

and

$$
D^2\le1024dr\le\frac{16384dt}{k}\le\frac{32768d\tau p^2}{k}.
$$

The hypothesis $k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2$ therefore gives $D/k<1/5000$. Since $r\ge p+1$ by P2 and every line vertex has degree at most $p$, one has

$$
D<k\le p<r.
$$

KTZ Lemma 2.2 supplies at least $D^3/(64d)$ eligible monomials of weighted degree at most $D$. Each identity imposed by a selected line contributes at most $D+1$ homogeneous coefficient constraints. Since

$$
\frac{D^3}{64d}>r(D+1),
$$

there is a nonzero interpolant satisfying all $r$ identities.

If the interpolant were independent of $Z$, each of the $r>D$ distinct selected affine lines would be a linear factor of a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$, which is impossible. The eligible monomials have $Z$-exponent zero or a positive $Z$-exponent not divisible by $p$; hence $Z$-dependence implies that the formal derivative $A_Z$ is nonzero. Choosing an interpolant of minimum weighted degree and applying the reductions in KTZ Lemmas 2.3 and 2.5 makes $A$ squarefree.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1 and P2, put $r=|R|$ and

$$
D=16\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{dr}\right\rfloor+1\right).
$$

There exists a nonzero squarefree polynomial $A\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree at most $D$ for weights $(1,1,d)$ such that

$$
A_Z\not\equiv0
$$

and

$$
A(M(s),P_M(s))\equiv0\qquad\text{for every }M\in R,
$$

where $M(s)$ is an affine parametrization of $M$. Moreover,

$$
D^2>256dr,
\qquad
D^2\le1024dr\le\frac{16384dt}{k}\le\frac{32768d\tau p^2}{k},
\qquad
\frac{D}{k}<\frac1{5000},
$$

so $D<k\le p<r$ and $D=O\!\left(\sqrt{d\tau p^2/k}\right)$.
lemmas.title: Trivariate Explainer

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix $L\in T$. If an accepted point $x\in N_G(L)$ is reached by some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$, then

$$
P_L(x)=f(x)=P_M(x).
$$

The sampled-line identity gives $A(x,P_M(x))=0$, and hence $A(x,P_L(x))=0$. By P2, this holds at more than half of the accepted neighbors of $L$, so the univariate polynomial

$$
s\longmapsto A(L(s),P_L(s))
$$

has more than $k/2>D$ distinct roots. Its degree is at most $D$, and it must therefore vanish identically. This argument applies to every $L\in T$ and incurs no averaging or Markov loss.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$, $R$, $A$, and $D$ satisfy the hypotheses and conclusions of P2 and P3. Then, for every $L\in T$ and every affine parametrization $L(s)$,

$$
A(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0.
$$
lemmas.title: Linewise Extension

lemmas.proof_markdown:
At most $D$ affine lines can make $H(L(s))$ vanish identically, because each such line contributes a distinct linear factor of $H$ and $\deg H\le D$. On any other line, the identity from P4 reads

$$
H(L(s))B(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0.
$$

Since $\mathbb{F}_p[s]$ is an integral domain and $H(L(s))$ is nonzero, exact polynomial division gives $B(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0$.

The quotient $B$ is squarefree and has degree below $p$. Since $\mathbb{F}_p$ is perfect, an irreducible factor whose three formal partial derivatives all vanish would be a nontrivial power with exponent $p$, which is impossible here. KTZ Lemma 2.4 therefore supplies a formal directional derivative $\mathcal{D}$ satisfying $\gcd(B,\mathcal{D}B)=1$.

KTZ Lemma 2.6 applies the relevant resultant to bound by $D(D-1)$ the lines on whose polynomial graphs both $B$ and $\mathcal{D}B$ vanish identically. On every other nontrivial line, the restricted derivative is a nonzero univariate polynomial of degree at most $D$, so it has at most $D$ accepted zeros. The trivial and degenerate lines contribute at most

$$
pD+pD(D-1)=pD^2
$$

edges, and all remaining lines contribute at most $Dt$. Thus $|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+Dt$. The argument uses a resultant rather than a discriminant.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P4, write

$$
A=\sum_j a_j(X,Y)Z^j,
\qquad
H(X,Y)=\gcd_j a_j(X,Y),
\qquad
B=A/H.
$$

Then $B$ is squarefree, has total degree less than $p$, and satisfies

$$
B(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0
$$

for every $L\in T$ such that $H(L(s))\not\equiv0$. There exists a formal directional derivative $\mathcal{D}$ such that

$$
\gcd(B,\mathcal{D}B)=1.
$$

Define

$$
T_{\mathrm{triv}}=\{L\in T:H(L(s))\equiv0\}
$$

and

$$
T_{\mathrm{deg}}=
\left\{L\in T\setminus T_{\mathrm{triv}}:(\mathcal{D}B)(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0\right\}.
$$

Then

$$
|T_{\mathrm{triv}}|\le D,
\qquad
|T_{\mathrm{deg}}|\le D(D-1),
$$

and every $L\in T\setminus(T_{\mathrm{triv}}\cup T_{\mathrm{deg}})$ satisfies

$$
\left|\{x\in N_G(L):(\mathcal{D}B)(x,f(x))=0\}\right|\le D.
$$

Consequently, for

$$
E_{\mathrm{exc}}=
\left\{(x,L)\in E:L\in T_{\mathrm{triv}}\cup T_{\mathrm{deg}}
\text{ or }(\mathcal{D}B)(x,f(x))=0\right\},
$$

one has

$$
|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+Dt.
$$
lemmas.title: Exceptional-Root Cleanup

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Since every line vertex of $G$ has degree at least $k$,

$$
|E|\ge kt.
$$

Using P5 and the bound $D^2\le16384dt/k$ from P3 gives

$$
\frac{|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|}{|E|}
\le\frac{pD^2+Dt}{|E|}
\le\frac{D}{k}+\frac{16384dp}{k^2}
<\frac1{4000}.
$$

During peeling, each removed vertex accounts for fewer than $k_1$ edges present at its removal. The original minimum-degree condition on both vertex classes gives

$$
k(|X|+t)\le2|E|.
$$

Thus peeling removes fewer than

$$
k_1(|X|+t)
\le2\frac{k_1}{k}|E|
\le\frac{|E|}{50}
$$

additional edges. Together with the exceptional-edge bound, this is less than $|E|$, so at least one edge remains. The remaining graph has minimum degree at least $k_1$ by construction. It need not remain connected and may split into several components.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P5,

$$
\frac{|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|}{|E|}
\le\frac{D}{k}+\frac{16384dp}{k^2}
<\frac1{4000}.
$$

Set

$$
k_1=\left\lfloor\frac{k}{100}\right\rfloor.
$$

Starting from $(X,T,E\setminus E_{\mathrm{exc}})$ and iteratively deleting every vertex whose current degree is less than $k_1$ removes fewer than

$$
k_1(|X|+t)
\le2\frac{k_1}{k}|E|
\le\frac{|E|}{50}
$$

additional edges and leaves a nonempty subgraph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $k_1$.
lemmas.title: Clean Core

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The numerical hypotheses give $k_1\ge2$. Fix $x\in X_1$ and choose two distinct incident lines $L_1,L_2\in T_1$. Their direction vectors $v_1,v_2$ are linearly independent, since two distinct affine lines through one point have distinct directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^2$.

Choose parametrizations $L_i(s)=x+sv_i$. Differentiating the formal identities

$$
B(L_i(s),P_{L_i}(s))\equiv0
$$

at $s=0$ gives

$$
v_{i,X}B_X(x,f(x))+v_{i,Y}B_Y(x,f(x))
+B_Z(x,f(x))P_{L_i}'(0)=0
$$

for $i\in\{1,2\}$. If $B_Z(x,f(x))=0$, the independence of $v_1$ and $v_2$ forces

$$
B_X(x,f(x))=B_Y(x,f(x))=0.
$$

All three formal partial derivatives would then vanish at $(x,f(x))$, implying $(\mathcal{D}B)(x,f(x))=0$. This contradicts the deletion rule defining $G_1$. Hence $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$. No derivative of a line polynomial is divided by in this argument.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ be the surviving graph from P6, and let $B$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be as in P5. Then every $x\in X_1$ satisfies

$$
B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad
B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.
$$
lemmas.title: Simple Roots

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Choose any connected component $C$ of $G_1$. Its minimum degree is at least $k_1$, and the numerical bounds give $k_1>D$. KTZ Lemmas 2.7 and 6.1 lift the line roots through one point of $C$ to a single polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$. Every division in the Newton lift is by a value $B_Z(b,f(b))$, which is a nonzero field element by P7; all global polynomials produced by the lift retain total degree at most $d$.

Simple-root uniqueness propagates the same $Q$ throughout $C$, as in KTZ Lemma 6.3, without a factor-count loss. Thus $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex of $C$.

The first numerical hypothesis also implies

$$
\frac1{\sqrt{p+1}}\le\frac{k_1}{4p}.
$$

Applying the mixing argument of KTZ Lemma 6.2 to $C$ gives

$$
\frac{|X_C|}{p^2}\ge\frac{k_1}{4p}\ge\frac{k}{800p}.
$$

Since $Q=f$ on $X_C$, this is the asserted global agreement.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1–P7, there exists a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.
$$
lemmas.title: Polynomial Decoder

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The threshold implies that the pruned minimum-degree parameter satisfies

$$
k_0\ge\frac{\epsilon p}{200}.
$$

Squaring the threshold gives

$$
\epsilon^2p\ge8{,}000{,}000C_*\Lambda d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
k_0^2\ge C_*dp
$$

and

$$
k_0^3\ge C_*d(\Lambda\epsilon)p^2\ge C_*d\tau p^2.
$$

The component decoder established in P1–P8 therefore applies with $k=k_0$ and yields

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]
\ge\frac{k_0}{800p}
\ge\frac{\epsilon}{160000}.
$$

This is the square-root parameter calculation. The entry remains conditional because local agreement alone has not supplied the assumed component with $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let

$$
\epsilon=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)],
$$

where $L$ is uniform among all affine lines of $\mathbb{F}_p^2$ and $x$ is uniform on $L$. Let $G_0$ be a graph supplied by KTZ Lemma 3.1 with minimum degree at least

$$
k_0=\left\lfloor\frac{\epsilon p}{100}\right\rfloor.
$$

Let $\Lambda\ge1$, and suppose $G_0$ has a connected component of line measure $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$. Put $C_*=2^{40}$ and assume

$$
\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000C_*\Lambda}\left(\frac{d}{p}\right)^{1/2}.
$$

Then there exists $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{\epsilon}{160000}.
$$
lemmas.title: Small-Component Corollary

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Independently color every point and every affine line uniformly from $[K]$, and choose an injection $\iota:[K]\hookrightarrow\mathbb{F}_p$. Set $f(x)$ equal to the embedded color of $x$, and let $P_L$ be the constant embedded color of $L$.

Conditional on a vertex color, the accepted degree of a line has distribution

$$
\operatorname{Bin}\!\left(p,\frac1K\right),
$$

while the accepted degree of a point has distribution

$$
\operatorname{Bin}\!\left(p+1,\frac1K\right).
$$

A Chernoff bound and a union bound over fewer than $3p^2$ vertices show that the probability of any asserted degree bound failing is at most

$$
6p^2e^{-p/(12K)}<1,
$$

where the last inequality follows from $p/K\ge100\log p$. Hence a deterministic realization satisfying every degree bound exists. Averaging the line-degree bounds and dividing by $p$ gives the stated interval for $\epsilon$. Every $P_L$ has degree $0$, hence degree at most the campaign degree $d>100$; the construction does not assert a separate analysis of the excluded parameter choice $d=0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p\ge103$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let $K$ be an integer satisfying

$$
2\le K\le\frac{p}{100\log p}.
$$

There exist a function $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$ and a constant polynomial $P_L$ on every affine line $L$ such that, with

$$
\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(L)=|\{x\in L:P_L(x)=f(x)\}|
$$

and

$$
\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(x)=|\{L\ni x:P_L(x)=f(x)\}|,
$$

one has, for every affine line $L$ and every point $x$,

$$
\frac{p}{2K}\le\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(L)\le\frac{2p}{K},
$$

$$
\frac{p+1}{2K}\le\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(x)\le\frac{2(p+1)}{K}.
$$

The test agreement satisfies

$$
\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K.
$$
lemmas.title: Balanced-Color Realization

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The line-degree upper bound gives

$$
|S_R|\le\sum_{M\in R}\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(M)
\le\frac{2p|R|}{K}.
$$

The covering hypothesis and the line-degree lower bound imply that every affine line contributes at least $p/(4K)$ accepted incidences from $S_R$. Summing over all $p(p+1)$ affine lines gives at least

$$
\frac{p^2(p+1)}{4K}
$$

such incidences. On the other hand, the point-degree upper bound permits at most $2(p+1)/K$ accepted incidences per point of $S_R$. Therefore

$$
|S_R|\ge\frac{p^2}{8}.
$$

Combining the two estimates yields $|R|\ge Kp/16$. Since P10 gives $\epsilon\ge1/(2K)$,

$$
\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon}.
$$

Finally, $f$ assumes at most $K$ color values. By pigeonhole, one constant value occurs on at least a $1/K$ fraction of all points. The corresponding constant polynomial has agreement at least $1/K\ge\epsilon/2$, using the upper bound $\epsilon\le2/K$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $f$ and the line table be as in P10. For a set $R$ of affine lines, define

$$
S_R=\{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2:\exists\,M\in R\text{ with }x\in M\text{ and }P_M(x)=f(x)\}.
$$

Suppose that every affine line $L$ satisfies

$$
\left|S_R\cap\{x\in L:P_L(x)=f(x)\}\right|
\ge\frac12\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(L).
$$

Then

$$
|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon}.
$$

Moreover, there exists a constant polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac1K\ge\frac{\epsilon}{2}.
$$
lemmas.title: Covering Lower Bound

lemmas.proof_markdown: Write $U=\sum_{i=0}^{r}a_i(X,Y)Z^i$ and $V=\sum_{j=0}^{s}b_j(X,Y)Z^j$. Weighted degree gives $\deg a_i\le u-di$ and $\deg b_j\le v-dj$. Every monomial in the Sylvester determinant contains $s$ coefficients of $U$ and $r$ coefficients of $V$, and the sum of their $Z$-indices is $rs$. The latter identity also follows from $\operatorname{Res}_Z(U(X,Y,TZ),V(X,Y,TZ))=T^{rs}\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V)$. Hence every determinant term has $(X,Y)$-degree at most $su+rv-drs$. Finally, $u-dr\ge0$ and $v-ds\ge0$, so $su+rv-drs=\frac{uv}{d}-\frac{(u-dr)(v-ds)}{d}\le\frac{uv}{d}$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and $d\ge1$. Give $\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ the weights $\operatorname{wt}(X)=\operatorname{wt}(Y)=1$ and $\operatorname{wt}(Z)=d$. Let $U,V\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be nonzero and coprime, with weighted degrees $u,v$ and $Z$-degrees $r,s$, respectively, where at least one of $r,s$ is positive. Then $$\deg_{X,Y}\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V)\le su+rv-drs=\frac{uv}{d}-\frac{(u-dr)(v-ds)}{d}\le\frac{uv}{d}.$$
lemmas.title: Weighted Sylvester degree

lemmas.proof_markdown: Coprimality makes $R=\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V)$ nonzero. When $r,s>0$, specialization along a graph gives the common root $q_L(t)$ over $\mathbb F_p(t)$, and therefore $R(L(t))\equiv0$. The affine-linear equation defining $L$ consequently divides $R$. Distinct lines yield pairwise nonassociate irreducible linear factors, so the number of lines is at most $\deg R$, which is at most $uv/d$ by the weighted Sylvester-degree bound. Since the number of lines is integral, it is at most $\left\lfloor uv/d\right\rfloor$. If, for example, $s=0$, then $V(L(t))\equiv0$ directly, so the number of lines is at most $\deg V\le v\le uv/d$, because $r>0$ implies $u\ge d$. The case $r=0$ is symmetric. Degree-dropping specializations cause no difficulty because the resultant is used without division by a leading coefficient.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses of the weighted Sylvester-degree lemma, let $\mathcal T$ be a family of distinct affine lines in $\mathbb F_p^2$. For every $L\in\mathcal T$, let $q_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ have degree at most $d$ and suppose $$U(L(t),q_L(t))\equiv V(L(t),q_L(t))\equiv0.$$ Then $$|\mathcal T|\le\left\lfloor\frac{uv}{d}\right\rfloor.$$
lemmas.title: Common graph-line count

lemmas.proof_markdown: An unknown polynomial supported on the $N_d(D)$ weighted monomials restricts on each graph to a univariate polynomial of degree at most $D$. Requiring this restriction to vanish identically imposes at most $D+1$ homogeneous linear equations. Thus the $n$ graph identities impose at most $n(D+1)<N_d(D)$ equations and admit a nonzero solution $A$. If $A$ were independent of $Z$, it would be a bivariate polynomial of degree at most $D$ vanishing identically on more than $D$ distinct affine lines. Every corresponding line equation would divide $A$, which is impossible. Hence $A$ depends on $Z$. Every positive $Z$-exponent occurring in $A$ is at most $\lfloor D/d\rfloor<p$ and is therefore nonzero in $\mathbb F_p$; consequently $A_Z\ne0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $1\le d\le D<p$. Let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines in $\mathbb F_p^2$, and assign to each $L\in\mathcal R$ a polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$. Define $$N_d(D)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor D/d\rfloor}\binom{D-dk+2}{2}.$$ If $n>D$ and $N_d(D)>n(D+1)$, then there exists a nonzero $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree at most $D$ such that $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0\qquad(L\in\mathcal R),$$ and $A$ depends on $Z$ with $A_Z\ne0$.
lemmas.title: Weighted graph interpolation

lemmas.proof_markdown: Existence and $Z$-dependence follow from the interpolation lemma. Suppose $A=P^eR$ for an irreducible $P$, with $e\ge2$ and $P\nmid R$. On each graph, $P(L(t),P_L(t))^eR(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ in the integral domain $\mathbb F_p[t]$. Hence $P(L(t),P_L(t))R(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ there as well. The polynomial $PR$ remains $Z$-dependent and has smaller weighted degree than $A$, contradicting minimality. Thus $A$ is squarefree. Dividing by the coefficient content $H$ makes $B$ primitive in $Z$ and preserves squarefreeness. If $H(L(t))\not\equiv0$, then $H(L(t))B(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ in $\mathbb F_p[t]$, so $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p,d,D,\mathcal R$, and $\{P_L\}_{L\in\mathcal R}$ satisfy the hypotheses of the weighted graph-interpolation lemma. Among the nonzero polynomials satisfying all graph identities, let $A$ have minimum weighted degree. Then $A$ is $Z$-dependent and squarefree. If $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content of $A$ as a polynomial in $Z$, then $B$ is primitive in $Z$ and squarefree. Moreover, for every $L\in\mathcal R$ with $H(L(t))\not\equiv0$, $$B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$
lemmas.title: Primitive squarefree reduction

lemmas.proof_markdown: Factor $B$ into distinct irreducibles. If an irreducible factor $C$ divided both $B$ and $B_Z$, write $B=CE$ with $C\nmid E$. Reducing $B_Z=C_ZE+CE_Z$ modulo $C$ shows that $C\mid C_Z$. Since differentiation lowers the $Z$-degree, this forces $C_Z=0$. Moreover, $\deg_ZC\le\deg_ZB\le D/d<p$. In characteristic $p$, a polynomial of $Z$-degree below $p$ with zero ordinary $Z$-derivative is independent of $Z$. Thus $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$, so $C$ divides every coefficient of $B$ as a polynomial in $Z$, contradicting primitivity. Therefore no common irreducible factor exists. Absolute irreducibility is neither assumed nor used.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $1\le d\le D<p$. Give $\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ the weights $(1,1,d)$. If $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ is $Z$-dependent, squarefree, primitive as a polynomial in $Z$, and has weighted degree at most $D$, then $$\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$
lemmas.title: Vertical separability

lemmas.proof_markdown: Put $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}B$ and $r=\deg_ZB$. Then $r<p$, $\operatorname{wdeg}B_Z\le\delta-d$, and $\deg_ZB_Z=r-1$. Vertical separability makes $B$ and $B_Z$ coprime. Applying the weighted resultant calculation to them bounds the identically ramified, non-content-trivial graph lines by $$\Delta=(2r-1)\delta-dr^2=\frac{\delta^2}{d}-\delta-\frac{(\delta-dr)^2}{d}\le\frac{\delta^2}{d}-\delta.$$ Let $a=\operatorname{wdeg}A$ and $h=\deg H$, so $a=h+\delta\le D$. At most $h$ distinct affine lines are content-trivial. Hence $$h+\Delta\le a-\delta+\frac{\delta^2}{d}-\delta\le\frac{a^2}{d}-a\le\frac{D^2}{d}-D.$$ The middle inequality follows from $$\frac{a^2}{d}-a-\left(a+\frac{\delta^2}{d}-2\delta\right)=(a-\delta)\left(\frac{a+\delta}{d}-2\right)\ge0,$$ using $a\ge\delta\ge d$. On every other graph, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $\delta-d\le D-d$, so ordinary root counting gives at most $D-d$ roots. An exceptional line contributes at most $p$ incidences. Dividing the resulting counts by the total $p^2(p+1)$ affine point-line incidences gives the stated loss.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and $1\le d\le D<p$. Let $A=HB\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ have weighted degree at most $D$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the $Z$-content and $B$ is $Z$-dependent, primitive, and squarefree. Let $\mathcal T$ be a family of distinct affine lines, each carrying $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$, such that $A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. Call $L$ content-trivial when $H(L(t))\equiv0$ and identically ramified when $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. Then at most $$\left\lfloor\frac{D^2}{d}-D\right\rfloor$$ lines in $\mathcal T$ are content-trivial or identically ramified. Every other $L\in\mathcal T$ contains at most $D-d$ values $t\in\mathbb F_p$ satisfying $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))=0$. Under uniform affine point-line sampling, deleting all these lines and points loses incidence mass at most $$\frac{D^2/d-D}{p(p+1)}+\frac{D-d}{p}.$$
lemmas.title: Vertical ramification cleanup

lemmas.proof_markdown: At a point where $B_Z(\mathbf b,\alpha)\ne0$, two distinct irreducible factors of the squarefree polynomial $B$ cannot both vanish, since their simultaneous vanishing would force $B_Z(\mathbf b,\alpha)=0$. Thus exactly one factor $C$ vanishes, and $C_Z(\mathbf b,\alpha)\ne0$. For each supplied graph, the factorization of $B(L(t),P_L(t))$ in the domain $\mathbb F_p[t]$ forces some irreducible factor to vanish identically. Evaluation at $t=0$ shows that this factor must be $C$. Newton recursion at $(\mathbf b,\alpha)$ produces the unique total-degree-at-most-$d$ truncation $Q$ through $\alpha$ and divides only by the nonzero field element $C_Z(\mathbf b,\alpha)$. Uniqueness makes $Q(L(t))=P_L(t)$ on every supplied line. The polynomial $C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))$ has total degree at most $\delta_C$ and vanishes identically on more than $\delta_C$ distinct lines, so it is zero. Finally, the kernel of substitution $Z\mapsto Q(X,Y)$ is $(Z-Q)$; irreducibility therefore makes $C$ associated to $Z-Q$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $B$ be a primitive squarefree polynomial as in the vertical-separability lemma. Suppose $(\mathbf b,\alpha)\in\mathbb F_p^2\times\mathbb F_p$ satisfies $B(\mathbf b,\alpha)=0$ and $B_Z(\mathbf b,\alpha)\ne0$. Then there is a unique irreducible factor $C$ of $B$ vanishing at $(\mathbf b,\alpha)$. Set $\delta_C=\operatorname{wdeg}C$. Suppose more than $\delta_C$ distinct affine lines through $\mathbf b$, parameterized by $L(0)=\mathbf b$, carry polynomials $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ satisfying $\deg P_L\le d$, $P_L(0)=\alpha$, and $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. Then there exists $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$Q(L(t))=P_L(t)$$ on every supplied line and $$C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0.$$ Moreover, $C$ is associated to $Z-Q$.
lemmas.title: Component-sensitive lifting

lemmas.proof_markdown: Conditionally retaining KTZ Lemmas 3.1–4.3 and 6.1–6.3, substitute the weighted graph interpolation and vertical ramification cleanup for the corresponding interpolation and Section 5 cleanup. The new deletion bound fits within the existing KTZ Lemma 4.1 budget. The remaining accepted graph therefore has the same minimum degrees and incidence mass required by the cited lifting, mixing, and component-propagation lemmas, which yield a polynomial $Q$ with global agreement at least $\varepsilon/8000$. The interpolation scale satisfies $D=O(\!\sqrt{dp/\varepsilon})$, while the surviving point loss obeys $$\frac{D-d}{p}=O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d}{\varepsilon p}}+\frac1p\right).$$ Requiring this loss to be $O(\varepsilon)$ is, up to constants in the cited parameter regime, equivalent to $\varepsilon^3\gtrsim d/p$. Thus the substitution preserves, but does not improve, the cubic exponent.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d\le p-1$, and let $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$ and degree-at-most-$d$ line labels $\{P_L\}$ have uniform point-line incidence agreement $\varepsilon$. Assume the hypotheses and conclusions of KTZ Lemmas 3.1–4.3 and 6.1–6.3 apply, with the weighted graph interpolation and vertical ramification cleanup used at their corresponding stages. If $\varepsilon\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}$ for a sufficiently large absolute constant $C$, then there exists $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{\varepsilon}{8000}.$$
lemmas.title: KTZ chain substitution

lemmas.proof_markdown: Ambient Hasse multiplicity $s$ at one lifted point imposes $\binom{s+2}{3}$ linear jet conditions. For $D\ge d\ge101$, $$\dim W_D=N_d(D)\le\frac{2D^3}{d},\qquad \binom{s+2}{3}\ge\frac{s^3}{6}.$$ Therefore $M\binom{s+2}{3}<\dim W_D$ implies $(D/s)^3>Md/12$. Hasse multiplicity may be defined through powers of the lifted maximal ideal, so no factorial division is used; after substitution into a line graph, that ideal maps into $(t-t_0)$ and produces a univariate root of multiplicity at least $s$. Root propagation consequently requires $sk>D$. Thus $k>D/s$ and $k^3>Md/12$. If $M\ge\rho p^2$ and $k\le K\varepsilon p$, comparison gives $K^3\varepsilon^3p^3>\rho p^2d/12$, which is the claimed cubic lower bound. This argument does not rule out dependent constraints, nonuniform multiplicities, or directional jets.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $D\ge d\ge101$. Let $W_D$ be the space of polynomials in $\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of $(1,1,d)$-weighted degree at most $D$. Suppose ambient Hasse multiplicity $s\ge1$ is imposed at $M$ lifted points and existence is certified by $$M\binom{s+2}{3}<\dim W_D.$$ If multiplicity root counting on a target graph containing $k$ interpolated points requires $sk>D$, then $$k^3>\frac{Md}{12}.$$ In particular, if $M\ge\rho p^2$ and $k\le K\varepsilon p$, then $$\varepsilon^3>\frac{\rho}{12K^3}\frac{d}{p}.$$
lemmas.title: Uniform multiplicity barrier

lemmas.proof_markdown: This claim is refuted by taking $p=409$, $d=101$, $D=202$, and $B=Z^2-XY$. The polynomial $B$ is primitive, irreducible, squarefree, and satisfies $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$ and $\operatorname{wdeg}B=202<409$. At $(0,0,0)$, however, $B_Z=0$ while $\partial_Z^{[2]}B=1$. For each projective direction $[a:b]$ for which $ab$ is a square, choose $c\in\mathbb F_{409}$ with $c^2=ab$ and set $L(t)=(at,bt)$ and $P_L(t)=ct$. There are $$2+\frac{p-1}{2}=206>D$$ such directions, and every graph satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. Nevertheless, $B(X,Y,Q)=0$ would imply $Q^2=XY$. This is impossible in the unique factorization domain $\mathbb F_{409}[X,Y]$, because the exponent of the irreducible factor $X$ is even in a square and odd in $XY$. Thus no polynomial $Q$ of any degree satisfies the asserted conclusion.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and $1\le d\le D<p$. Let $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be primitive, irreducible, squarefree, and of $(1,1,d)$-weighted degree at most $D$, with $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Let $(\mathbf b,\alpha)$ satisfy $B(\mathbf b,\alpha)=B_Z(\mathbf b,\alpha)=0$ and $\partial_Z^{[j]}B(\mathbf b,\alpha)\ne0$ for some $j\ge2$. If more than $D$ distinct affine lines through $\mathbf b$, parameterized by $L(0)=\mathbf b$, carry polynomials $P_L$ with $\deg P_L\le d$, $P_L(0)=\alpha$, and $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, then there exists $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $Q(L(t))=P_L(t)$ on all supplied lines and $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0$.
lemmas.title: Higher-Hasse lifting claim

lemmas.proof_markdown: Choose $f$ uniformly at random. For a fixed total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$, the number of points on which $f$ and $Q$ agree has distribution $\operatorname{Bin}(p^2,1/p)$ and mean $p$. A Chernoff bound gives $$\Pr\!\left[\Pr_x[f(x)=Q(x)]\ge\frac4p\right]\le e^{-(4\log4-3)p}.$$ There are at most $p^N$ such formal polynomials. The displayed hypothesis therefore makes the union-bound probability strictly less than one, yielding a table $f$ whose agreement with every $Q$ is below $4/p$. On each affine line, interpolate the values of $f$ at any $d+1$ distinct points by a polynomial of degree at most $d$. Every line label then agrees at at least $(d+1)/p$ of its points, so the same lower bound holds under uniform affine-line sampling. Along any growing choice $d=o(\sqrt{p/\log p})$, the global-to-local ratio is below $4/(d+1)$ and tends to zero. For every fixed $\alpha>1$, the local scale $d/p$ eventually dominates every fixed multiple of $(d/p)^\alpha$, proving the asserted exponent ceiling. This does not obstruct an exponent of $1-o(1)$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d\le p-1$, and set $N=\binom{d+2}{2}$. If $$N\log p<(4\log4-3)p,$$ then there exist a point table $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$ and degree-at-most-$d$ labels on every affine line such that their uniform local agreement $\varepsilon$ satisfies $$\varepsilon\ge\frac{d+1}{p},$$ while every $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]<\frac4p.$$ Consequently, for every fixed $\alpha>1$ and fixed positive constants $C,c$, there are arbitrarily large such instances with $\varepsilon\ge C(d/p)^\alpha$ but global agreement below $c\varepsilon$ for every total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial.
lemmas.title: Uniform-sampling exponent ceiling

lemmas.proof_markdown: This claim is refuted by the surviving nonexceptional root loss. Substituting $D=O(\sqrt{dp/\varepsilon})$ into the point bound from the vertical ramification cleanup gives $$\frac{D-d}{p}=O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d/p}{\varepsilon}}\right)$$ up to the lower-order endpoint term recorded in the application. Making this loss $O(\varepsilon)$ requires $$\sqrt{\frac{d/p}{\varepsilon}}\lesssim\varepsilon,$$ which is equivalent, up to absolute constants, to $$\varepsilon^3\gtrsim\frac{d}{p}.$$ Thus the algebraic improvement leaves the controlling exponent equal to $1/3$ rather than making it strictly larger.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d\le p-1$, let $0<\varepsilon\le1$, and let $d\le D<p$ satisfy $D=O(\sqrt{dp/\varepsilon})$. Then there exists an exponent $\alpha>1/3$ such that the hypothesis $\varepsilon\gtrsim(d/p)^\alpha$ suffices, using the vertical ramification cleanup alone, to make its surviving loss $O(\varepsilon)$.
lemmas.title: Algebraic exponent-improvement claim

lemmas.proof_markdown: Because $(v_M,u_M)$ is a basis, the affine change from $(T,S)$ to $(X,Y)$ is invertible, and its inverse expresses $T$ and $S$ as affine-linear polynomials in $X$ and $Y$. The inverse third coordinate is $W=Z-P_M(T)$. Since $\deg P_M\le d$, both the substitution and its inverse preserve the filtration with weights $(1,1,d)$. Setting $S=W=0$ gives $(X,Y)=b_M+Tv_M$ and $Z=P_M(T)$, so the lifted graph ideal becomes $(S,W)$. No division by a derivative or factorial is involved.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $M(t)=b_M+tv_M$ be an affine line in $\mathbb F_p^2$ with a polynomial $P_M\in\mathbb F_p[T]$ satisfying $\deg P_M\le d$. Choose $u_M\in\mathbb F_p^2$ such that $(v_M,u_M)$ is a basis. Give $T$ and $S$ weight $1$ and $W$ weight $d$. Then

$$
(X,Y)=b_M+Tv_M+Su_M,\qquad Z=P_M(T)+W
$$

defines a filtered polynomial isomorphism between $\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ and $\mathbb F_p[T,S,W]$. Under this isomorphism, the defining ideal $I_M$ of the lifted graph of $P_M$ is $(S,W)$.
lemmas.title: Adapted normal coordinates

lemmas.proof_markdown:
By the filtered coordinate isomorphism, every $A\in V_D$ has a unique expansion

$$
A=\sum_{a,b\ge 0}c_{a,b}(T)S^aW^b,
$$

where $\deg c_{a,b}\le D-a-db$. Membership in $(S,W)^s$ is equivalent to $c_{a,b}=0$ whenever $a+b<s$. For each such pair, equating the coefficients of $T$ gives exactly $\max\{D-a-db+1,0\}$ independent scalar conditions. The corresponding residue classes of the monomials $T^iS^aW^b$ form a basis of the quotient by $(S,W)^s$, proving the one-line codimension formula. For $n$ lines, the rank of the combined system is at most the sum of the individual codimensions, namely $nC_s(D,d)$; dependencies between constraints from different lines can only reduce this rank.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $V_D\subseteq\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be the space of polynomials of weighted degree at most $D$ for weights $(1,1,d)$. For a lifted line-graph ideal $I_M$, define

$$
C_s(D,d)=\sum_{\substack{a,b\ge 0\\a+b<s}}\max\{D-a-db+1,0\}.
$$

Then $V_D\cap I_M^s$ has codimension exactly $C_s(D,d)$ in $V_D$. If $\mathcal R$ consists of $n$ distinct lifted line graphs, then the simultaneous conditions $A\in I_M^s$ for all $M\in\mathcal R$ impose at most $nC_s(D,d)$ homogeneous linear equations on $V_D$.
lemmas.title: Normal-jet codimension

lemmas.proof_markdown: For a fixed exponent $j$ of $Z$, the admissible monomials in $X$ and $Y$ have total degree at most $D-dj$ and therefore number $\binom{D-dj+2}{2}$. Summing over $0\le j\le\lfloor D/d\rfloor$ gives $\dim V_D=N_d(D)$. The common order-$s$ conditions have rank at most $nC_s(D,d)$. Thus $N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d)$ leaves a positive-dimensional kernel, which contains a nonzero common interpolant.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines equipped with polynomials of degree at most $d$. Define

$$
N_d(D)=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor D/d\rfloor}\binom{D-dj+2}{2}.
$$

If $N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d)$, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree at most $D$ such that $A\in I_M^s$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$.
lemmas.title: Jet interpolation

lemmas.proof_markdown: In coordinates adapted to $M$, a polynomial independent of $Z$ is also independent of $W$. Its membership in $(S,W)^s$ therefore forces divisibility by $S^s$. Since $S$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of the line equation $\ell_M$, the factor $\ell_M^s$ divides $A$. The equations of distinct affine lines are pairwise nonassociate prime linear polynomials, so their product to the $s$-th power divides $A$. As $A$ is independent of $Z$, its ordinary degree equals its weighted degree and is at most $D$. Hence $D\ge sn$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines. Let $A\ne 0$ have weighted degree at most $D$ and satisfy $A\in I_M^s$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$. For each $M\in\mathcal R$, let $\ell_M$ be a nonzero affine-linear equation defining $M$. If $A$ is independent of $Z$, then

$$
\prod_{M\in\mathcal R}\ell_M^s\mid A
$$

and $D\ge sn$. Consequently, if $D<sn$, then $A$ depends on $Z$.
lemmas.title: Line-factor divisibility

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Set $z=\deg_Z A$ and suppose $z<s$. After replacing $Z$ by $P_M(T)+W$, the degree in $W$ remains $z$. Membership in $(S,W)^s$ forces the coefficient of $W^j$ to be divisible by $S^{s-j}$ for every $0\le j\le z$. Hence every coefficient is divisible by $S^{s-z}$, so $\ell_M^{s-z}$ divides $A$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$. Distinctness of the lines then gives
